Verified in both directions before re-freezing: with the four fragments as shipped (empty 'services: {}' stubs) the test is RED for the correct reason, and with the four temporarily filled it is GREEN — so the amendment makes C1 reachable without making it free. No assertion was weakened, no test renamed, no test added or removed; the suite stays at 120. Only test_spec_criteria.py changed.

head: 4046ec68a0e3b210af785e0ea2caac832f1abd5d
reason:
ESC-005 / T-117, user-authorized by Hank directly in-session ("You have my authorization for all three of the proposed changes"). scripts/verify.sh only; goals.json and .swarm-loop/acceptance/ are untouched by this amend.

Two changes, neither weakening any assertion:

1. run_pytest now EMITS a SELECTION line after every invocation naming the deselected and skipped counts, with a note that those tests did not run. T-117 acceptance 2 ("deselected counts are reported, not swallowed, so a green gate names what it did not run"). Nothing is made easier to pass; a count is printed that was previously invisible.

2. `check` no longer deselects `docker`. That blanket deselection WAS the defect T-117 names: it silently removed all three of T-110's fresh-volume tests including the one grading that ticket's acceptance criterion 2, so a lane reported its own gate green while the tests written to grade it never ran. T-109 replaced the all-or-nothing datastore assumption with per-service reachability, so a docker-marked test now probes the service it needs and skips cleanly when that service is down. This is T-117 acceptance 1 and 3.

VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE AMENDING. Still passes with by-design deselection: `verify.sh check` -> exit 0, 3908 passed / 1 deselected (up from ~3520 selected, i.e. ~388 docker tests that every per-ticket gate had been silently dropping); `verify.sh all` -> exit 0, 3908 pytest / 710 vitest / mypy clean on 205 files. Still refuses a gate that selects nothing: pytest exits 5 when everything is deselected (measured: a marker matching nothing gives `801 deselected`, exit 5) and run_pytest maps exit 5 to a FATAL non-zero, a path unchanged by this amend apart from an added explanatory line.

NOT included: ESC-007's change to .swarm-loop/acceptance/test_e4_store_agent.py. It is written and compiles but the acceptance suite cannot be executed in this session (blocked by the auto-mode classifier; pyproject norecursedirs excludes .swarm-loop from pytest collection, so no other route reaches it), and an amend around bytes that were never run is exactly what this mechanism exists to prevent. That file is restored to its frozen bytes and ESC-007 stays open.

head: 6d8a27d028588d8c065a10ed65ad33f753d32b66
reason:
ESC-005 amendment 5 — CORRECTING amendment 4's own defects, found by a rung-2 verifier.
scripts/verify.sh only. Same user authorization; this fixes my implementation of it, and
corrects two false figures I recorded in amendment 4's justification.

1. THE REAL BUG. run_pytest's SELECTION parsing ran under `set -euo pipefail`:
   `line="$(grep -E ... | tail -1)"`. A grep that matches nothing exits 1, pipefail promotes
   it, and the assignment's non-zero status tripped errexit — killing the function before
   `return "$rc"`, before the SELECTION line, and before `rm -f`. A verifier drove both bodies
   through a replica of the call site and measured pytest's real exit code being destroyed:
   usage-error 4->1, INTERNALERROR 3->1, SIGKILL 137->1, interrupt 2->1, and a GREEN run whose
   epilogue could not be parsed 0->1. Fail-closed, so amendment 4 weakened nothing — but it
   discarded the true status, leaked the temp file, and suppressed the SELECTION line in exactly
   the case where the parse had failed. Fixed with `|| true` on the capture plus an explicit
   UNPARSEABLE branch that reports the unknown coverage and returns the real rc. Re-verified
   across all five modes: 4->4, 3->3, 137->137, 2->2, 0->0.

2. TWO FALSE FIGURES I RECORDED, corrected in place. Amendment 4 claimed "~3520 -> 3908, i.e.
   ~388 docker tests". Measured truth: old selection 3729 / 247 deselected, new 3975 / 1, so
   246 newly-run docker tests. My number compared a pre-cycle-11 suite size against a
   post-cycle-11 one and charged ~142 newly-ADDED tests to this change. Direction right,
   magnitude wrong by ~58%. And there is NO slow-marked test — `-m slow` collects zero — so
   "the single slow test" was wrong; the one remaining deselection is needs_model, before and
   after. `and not slow` is a present-day no-op.

3. THE UNNAMED THIRD BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE, now named in the file. Every `graph`-marked test is
   also `docker`-marked, so the old `check` never built the session-scoped `_neo4j_guard` and
   never took the machine-global flock. The new one does, and holds it for most of the run
   (measured: 196s of a 222s session). Concurrent lanes running `check` serialise on it, and one
   that waits past the budget fails with Neo4jLockTimeout for a machine reason. Tracked as its
   own ticket; the fix belongs in the fixture's scope, not in this file.

Also corrected: the usage header at line 5 still said `check` "skips @pytest.mark.docker and
.slow", which has been false since amendment 4 and is the first line a reader consults.

Verified after: verify.sh check exit 0, 3975 passed / 1 deselected.

reason:

THE DEFECT: the frozen metric build_succeeds is 'if PROXYSHOP_WORKER=0 make verify ...', and 130 ticket gates pinned the same worker. Under D38 that is the same Postgres database and the same Redis logical DB; conftest.py:424,430 calls flushdb() before AND after every test and the Postgres fixtures TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE across 29 tables. So a lane or a red-check running a gate while a measure is in flight does not produce a flaky test — it CORRUPTS A SCORED FROZEN METRIC whose history is the regression the loop steers on. cmd_measure runs with no lock, no quiesce and nothing serialising it against dispatch; the harness's only lockfile guards state.json and explicitly never blocks.

MEASURED COST OF THE COLLISION, not asserted: two identical test_ledger_chain.py runs launched concurrently on the same worker index gave 13 failed/107 passed and 12 failed/108 passed; the same command solo immediately after gave 120/120. A same-index collision produces a spurious ~10% failure rate that looks exactly like flaky product code.

VALIDATED BEFORE APPLYING. 18 gates spanning every backing store — Postgres, Redis, Neo4j, pure-static, e2e, './scripts/verify.sh check', and 'make verify' itself — were run BOTH WAYS, serially, 36 runs. ZERO differences: 16 of 18 pairs byte-identical after normalising wall-clock times, the other two differing only in a vitest duration line and a Python object address. The four RED gates fail on the same assertion text and the same failing node ids on both workers. make verify on worker 15: rc=0, 5490 passed, 'OK: all'.

WORKER 15 IS GENUINELY UNCLAIMED AND ALREADY PROVISIONED: proxyshop_w15 has 29 tables and the same four applied migrations and seed rows as proxyshop_w0, zero live sessions before and after; Redis logical DB 15 has DBSIZE 0 and an empty keyspace; no worktree declares it and no committed file mentions it. Provisioning-on-demand was demonstrated separately on worker 11, which went from 0 tables to 29 with 178/178 passing in one gate run.

FIELD-SCOPED ON PURPOSE, and this is the part a naive edit gets wrong: a text substitution over the file changes 148 lines, of which 18 are NOT verify fields — they are 'objective' and 'reproduction' PROSE that also contains PROXYSHOP_WORKER=0. That would silently push this outside the pre-approved verify-field class. The edit iterates ticket objects and rewrites t['verify'] only; exactly 130 fields, each with exactly one occurrence (68 prefix-form, 62 export-form), no gate embeds a literal proxyshop_w0 or w0: string, and the 18 prose occurrences are verified still present and untouched afterwards.

A LITERAL 15 RATHER THAN 0, deliberately, and the reasoning is the point. The default-expansion form was measured viable and would ALSO fix lane-vs-lane collisions, because each lane would resolve to its own exported id. But red-check runs gates through subprocess Popen(shell=True) with no env=, so a gate inheriting the caller's environment resolves to whatever the ORCHESTRATOR has exported — which is 0 — re-introducing the exact gate-vs-measure collision this amendment exists to remove, at the one call site that matters most. A literal cannot be defeated by a caller's environment. The unconditional guarantee is worth more here than the extra class it would close.

THE RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: gate-vs-gate collisions remain. Nothing assigns or reserves worker ids — worker.py says so itself, there is no worker field in any of the 267 dispatch.jsonl records, and check-wave vetoes overlapping FILE ownership, which has no relationship to datastore ownership. Two lanes each running its own ticket gate still both land on 15, and 25 of the 26 recorded red-check timestamps fall inside a window with 2-7 lanes open. That class exists identically today with all 130 on worker 0, so this amendment does not worsen it; what it removes entirely is the third and worst class, gate-vs-measure, which becomes structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely. Two further things no worker id can fix: Neo4j Community has ONE database and is isolated only by a machine-global flock, and .pytest_cache/.mypy_cache are shared by anything in the same checkout.
